name: Kristian Krattiger
hero_headline: Deterministic Verification, Control Gates & Evaluation for AI Systems
hero_subheadline: I build and test reliability gates, grounding pipelines, and data-backed systems where probabilistic models meet strict correctness and auditability constraints—publishing both what works and what fails under preregistered checks.
line: Deterministic verification, control gates, and evaluation for AI and data-backed systems.
description: Portfolio and evidence ledger of Kristian Krattiger — Applied AI Engineering, Systems Architecture, and Technology Risk. Probabilistic models propose; deterministic checks decide what gets admitted, executed, or recorded.
education: B.A. Business Administration (Information Systems), Minor in Computer Science — California State University, Fullerton (Senior)
resume_summary: Information Systems & Computer Science senior at CSUF building applied AI evaluation tools, relational databases, ETL pipelines, and operational applications across Python, SQL/SQLite, TypeScript, C++17, and C#/.NET. Experienced leading a multi-developer ERP database and Flask framework build, designing reproducible test harnesses, and documenting both working systems and measured failure modes. Targeting early-career roles in Applied AI Engineering, Systems Architecture, and Technology Risk / Consulting.
next: Completing my degree at CSUF, finishing the QSR ERP implementation, and targeting early-career roles in Applied AI Engineering, Systems Architecture, and Technology Risk / Consulting.
work_paragraph: Probabilistic systems are allowed to propose; deterministic systems decide what gets admitted, executed, or recorded. GIN is the architectural frame. SEAR, Receipts with Assay, Latch, and Backstop test specific verification and control gates under preregistered criteria.
Some gates held on bounded sets. Others failed or were killed under criteria written before running them. Both sides appear here with equal weight, linked directly to primary artifacts.

projects.name: GIN
projects.subtitle: Grounded Intelligence Network — decode-time grounding, sole-writer graph admission, and mTLS federation
projects.summary: Prevents ungrounded LLM claims by constraining token generation to verbatim corpus spans and gating all graph state mutations through a single structural Bookkeeper across mTLS-federated nodes.

case_study.problem: Standard RAG pipelines let language models fabricate unsupported claims, silently merge conflicting sources, or write unverified assertions directly into persistent knowledge graphs. GIN separates probabilistic proposal from deterministic admission across decode-time token constraints, a sole-writer graph Bookkeeper, and trust-gated peer routing.

flow.title: Local LLM & Cartographer
flow.detail: Retrieves candidate chunks and proposes continuations (Mistral-7B / Qwen2.5-7B) or inter-document relations.

flow.title: SEAR Mask + Bookkeeper + Trust Gate
flow.detail: Logits processor masks tokens outside verbatim corpus spans; Bookkeeper checks confidence floor, anchors, and DAG acyclicity; mTLS router checks peer domain trust.

flow.title: Provenance-Stamped State or Refusal
flow.detail: Admits provenance-stamped graph nodes and grounded answers, or emits an explicit refusal when out-of-scope or untrusted.

case_study.tradeoff: Verbatim decode constraints stopped token fabrication (0/21 on baseline, 0/50 adversarial decode trials), but cannot stop misleading juxtaposition or planted false sources (3/3 counterfactuals repeated). On the first all-layer stress run, production RRF peer selection dropped to 0.488 P@1, lexical-overlap verification accepted 15/16 adversarial probes, a forged peer chunk slipped through unverified, and issue-framing recall stayed 0/4 across 5 frozen encoders and 0/15 after patches.

open_questions.q: Does the relation detector hold on a corpus written by someone blind to its internals? (The 2026-11-22 stress set does not answer this: its author shaped both the set and the fixes.)
Do the stress-benchmark fixes hold on contradiction pairs and queries written after them?
open_questions.resolves: A fresh set written after the patches, ideally by someone who has not seen the detector; the patched code scored on it once, unchanged.

open_questions.q: Is issue-framing contradiction a detectable signal, or a curatorial stance that labels cannot pin down?
open_questions.resolves: More labeled pairs than four, ideally from more than one labeler.

open_questions.q: Do the federation bars survive nodes on separate machines?
open_questions.resolves: A multi-machine run of the same query sets.

projects.name: SEAR
projects.subtitle: Sparse Epistemically Anchored Reasoning — decode-time constraints (GIN) and verify-after claim gating (sear-demo)
projects.summary: Compares two grounding architectures for LLM outputs: blocking unsupported tokens during decoding (GIN) versus filtering free-form drafts through NLI entailment and exact name/number checks (sear-demo).
projects.meta: Python · phi-4 · DeBERTa-v3 NLI · Deterministic Span Checks

case_study.problem: Free-form RAG answers routinely blend retrieved facts with memorized claims, especially on near-miss or out-of-corpus queries. SEAR enforces that emitted claims trace back to retrieved chunks, replacing unsupported guesses with an explicit failure state.

flow.title: Draft Generation (phi-4)
flow.detail: Generates candidate claims citing retrieved chunks (or proposes tokens constrained by GIN's verbatim logits processor).

flow.title: NLI Entailment + Name/Number Check
flow.detail: Verifies chunk entailment with nli-deberta-v3-base and checks that every name and number appears verbatim in the cited chunk.

flow.title: Grounded Answer or Explicit Refusal
flow.detail: Emits only claims that clear both checks; when zero claims survive, returns an explicit failure state instead of guessing.

case_study.tradeoff: Refused 9/9 out-of-corpus and near-miss probes on a 27-probe smoke set, but over-refused 5 supportable probes (9/14 failure-state precision). Verification enforces the corpus rather than ground truth: poisoned chunks passed 5/5, and conflicting chunks were silently resolved to the model's parametric memory on 4/5 conflict probes (no conflict detector is built).

open_questions.q: Can the gate tell when two cited chunks contradict each other?
open_questions.resolves: A conflict detector, measured on the conflict fork.

open_questions.q: Which of the review's measurement gaps are fixed?
open_questions.resolves: The review document and a per-item status from the author.

open_questions.q: What happens when retrieval actually has to choose?
open_questions.resolves: A corpus large enough that top_k leaves most chunks out.

versions.name: SEAR in GIN: verify while generating
versions.how: A custom llama-cpp-python logits processor constrains every token at decode time to continue a span that occurs verbatim in the retrieved corpus. Text the corpus does not contain cannot be generated in the first place.
versions.where: These entries live on the GIN page and are counted under GIN.

versions.name: sear-demo: verify after generating
versions.how: The model writes freely. Each claim must then be entailed by its cited chunk (NLI), and every name and number must appear in that chunk, or the claim is dropped. When nothing survives, an explicit failure state replaces a guess.
versions.where: The rest of this page covers this version; the counts on this page and on Home are its entries only.

projects.name: Receipts + Assay
projects.subtitle: Claim-audit pipeline and standalone TypeScript verification library (Assay v0.1.0)
projects.summary: Audits vendor claims against independent regulatory filings (SEC, NHTSA, IIHS) by letting a model propose candidate contradictions while discarding any quote a deterministic byte-offset gate cannot re-find.
projects.meta: TypeScript · Byte-Offset Quote Gate · SEC / NHTSA / IIHS · Assay v0.1.0

case_study.problem: Automated due-diligence and compliance tools that summarize vendor pages with LLMs routinely hallucinate citations or silently omit sources they failed to fetch. Receipts and its extracted library Assay enforce verbatim byte-offset grounding and explicit 'not read' accounting.

flow.title: Source Fetch & Model Proposer
flow.detail: Fetches vendor pages alongside independent sources (SEC 10-K, NHTSA recalls, IIHS); an LLM proposes candidate claim-vs-source pairings.

flow.title: Assay Byte-Offset Substring Gate
flow.detail: Re-locates every quoted string verbatim in the fetched source bytes with exact offsets and discards unanchored quotes.

flow.title: Audited Ledger or Reasoned Refusal
flow.detail: Writes structured ledger rows (disputed, unverified, context_unverified) and explicitly records blocked sources as 'not read'.

case_study.tradeoff: Exact substring checks stop fabricated quotes but do not prove a quote is a fair reading—an earlier divergent Tesla row had to be removed after catching a truncated Wikipedia sentence. A frontier-model relation check denied 30/30 no-relation pairs but admitted only 2/5 real relations (left off by default); G2 (0/16 attempts) and Reddit could not be fetched and remain logged as 'not read'.

open_questions.q: Can any relation check, local or frontier, admit real relations without admitting same-topic noise?
open_questions.resolves: More than about four independent positive labels.

open_questions.q: What does 'testing Assay' still need to cover?

projects.name: Latch
projects.subtitle: Preregistered mechanical admission and provenance gates for small-model reasoning and tool calls
projects.summary: Tested whether typed-operator and tool-parameter provenance gates improve 3B–14B model reliability across three preregistered studies—documenting why abstention and false-alarm overhead killed or nulled every arm.
projects.meta: Python · Qwen2.5 3B–14B · 2WikiMultihopQA · BFCL v4 · Preregistered Studies

case_study.problem: Small models make silent reasoning errors and issue wrong state-changing tool calls. Latch tested whether forcing models through strict mechanical admission schemas and parameter-provenance gates beats unconstrained chain-of-thought or plain tool calling under preregistered pass/kill criteria.

flow.title: Small Model Proposal (Qwen2.5 3B–14B)
flow.detail: Emits formal operator steps (Studies 1–2 on 2WikiMultihopQA) or state-changing tool calls (Study 3 on BFCL multi-turn).

flow.title: Operator Schema & Provenance Gate
flow.detail: Validates typed operator contracts and checks whether state-changing tool parameters trace to verified prior context.

flow.title: Admit or Abstain / Block
flow.detail: Admits valid outputs or blocks/abstains on contract failure, evaluated strictly against preregistered McNemar and margin bars.

case_study.tradeoff: All three studies missed their preregistered promotion bars: the Study 1 pilot was killed at G3 (37.5% vs 80.6% CoT accuracy at full coverage due to 55.6% abstention); Study 2 agreement flagged errors (2.80% vs 9.47%) but failed to beat plain self-consistency (+0.32 pp, 95% CI [-0.90, +1.59]); Study 3 cut wrong state-changing actions across 3B/7B/14B but triggered 9.3%–33.5% false alarms and reduced task success by up to 5.3 pp.

open_questions.q: Does mechanical admission pay off only when a claim can be anchored to a literal artifact?
open_questions.resolves: A registered test on a gate that anchors to fetched bytes or export rows.

open_questions.q: Would a warning, or exempting values the model could look up, keep the catch without the false alarms?
open_questions.resolves: A new registered study (named in study 3's limitations).

open_questions.q: Does a gated chain of small models behave differently from one gated model?
open_questions.resolves: Running the multi-model arms, which no study so far has.

projects.name: Backstop + Diagnosis
projects.subtitle: Error-triggered stop gates and artifact-only diagnosis for small-model tool agents
projects.summary: Intercepts premature agent stops after unresolved tool errors and injects deterministic hints parsed strictly from error text and tool schemas (zero ground truth), audited under Holm-Bonferroni and harm guardrails.
projects.meta: Python · Ollama (Qwen2.5 / Llama3.1 / Gemma4 / Ministral) · BFCL · Holm-Bonferroni & Wilson Bounds

case_study.problem: Small tool-calling agents frequently give up right after a tool error instead of correcting the bad argument or missing prerequisite. Blindly forcing retries adds wrong actions; Backstop tests whether deterministic error+schema diagnosis turns runtime failure artifacts into safe recovery.

flow.title: Agent Premature Stop After Tool Error
flow.detail: Multi-turn tool agent (7B–9B) receives a runtime tool error and attempts to terminate the turn unresolved.

flow.title: Stop Gate + Artifact-Only diagnose()
flow.detail: Parses only the tool error string and active tool schema (zero ground truth) to decide whether an actionable repair hint exists.

flow.title: Refuse with Hint or Permit Stop (D_only)
flow.detail: Refuses premature stop with the deterministic diagnostic hint or permits clean termination; scored on H1/H2 lift plus G1/G2 harm ceilings.

case_study.tradeoff: Stage 1 bare stop refusals tripped both harm guardrails. Confirmatory diagnosis (N=843, qwen2.5:7b) lifted recovery from 16.0% to 42.1% and whole-task success by +5.7 pp with clean G1 (4.0%), but failed G2 (2.579x post-fork wrong actions) because of blind fallback turns. Dropping blind fallbacks (D_only, exploratory) eliminated regressions (49 rescued, 0 lost) and cut wrong actions 73–79%, yet gains did not transfer uniformly across families (null on ministral-3:8b, redundant on gemma4:e4b) and an external tau2-bench smoke gate failed below the zero-tool floor.

open_questions.q: Does the hint-only gate (D_only) preserve qwen2.5:7b's zero-regression lift on completely unseen seeds under a preregistered harm guardrail?
open_questions.resolves: A new preregistered run on untouched seeds (e.g., extension/pool_ext.jsonl tasks 251–500) paired with a call-normalized or risk-weighted guardrail.

open_questions.q: Does error+schema diagnosis transfer outside BFCL's eight simulated apps, and does it remain useful as stronger small models self-recover on bare refusals?
open_questions.resolves: An external tool-use benchmark where unmodified 7–9B models clear a zero-tool floor, tested across multiple model families.

projects.name: PriceRiot
projects.closed_note: Closed as v1 on 2026-11-25 (commit 650c8f4): headless C++17 simulation core, dynamic pricing elasticity, parameter-sweep API, held-out POS calibration & elasticity evaluations, and full-stack tests (27 pytest + 16 Vitest) are complete. Automated layout optimization (P3.9) and built-in ML (P4) are formally closed as out of scope.
projects.subtitle: C++17 discrete-event retail simulation core, dynamic pricing & sweeps API, POS ETL, and held-out calibration eval
projects.summary: Completed v1 retail simulation engine (C++17/pybind11 A* navmesh, dynamic price elasticity, parameter-sweep API, POS CSV ETL, FastAPI + Vue 3 / Streamlit) validated with held-out synthetic POS calibration, controlled pricing-elasticity sweeps, and 43 full-stack tests.
projects.meta: Completed v1 · C++17 · pybind11 · Python ETL · FastAPI + Vue 3 · Streamlit · 27 pytest / 16 Vitest

case_study.problem: Retail analytics, staffing, and pricing studies often lack repeatable transaction datasets tied to physical store layouts and deterministic controls. PriceRiot pairs a POS CSV parameter-extraction ETL with a headless C++17 discrete-event agent engine, dynamic SKU pricing, multi-run sweeps, and out-of-sample evaluation.

flow.title: POS CSV ETL, Pricing & YAML Spec
flow.detail: Cleans POS transaction exports, maps SKUs, fits arrival parameters out-of-sample, and configures YAML layouts, staffing, and SKU price multipliers.

flow.title: C++17 Engine, Elasticity & Sweeps
flow.detail: Runs deterministic A* navmesh agents with price-elasticity acceptance across typed pybind11 bindings, multi-day TemporalScheduler, and /api/sweeps.

flow.title: Calibrated Logs, Dashboards & Eval
flow.detail: Persists runs/sweeps to SQLite, exports CSVs to FastAPI/Vue 3 and Streamlit, and scores held-out calibration and elasticity invariants.

case_study.tradeoff: Held-out synthetic POS calibration matched 6 schedule-aligned Mon-Sat open days within -3.22% transactions and +4.03% revenue (0.0325 intraday TVD), and controlled price markups produced monotonic demand drops (-0.414 to -0.941 arc elasticity) with stable control SKUs. Because extract_params() transfers only spawn_interval_seconds, SKU top-10 overlap stayed at 38% and a Sunday schedule mismatch widened 7-day transaction error to -15.23%; fit to real (non-synthetic) store data is not tested. Automated layout optimization (P3.9) and built-in ML (P4) are formally closed as out of scope for v1.

artifacts.label: C++17 pybind11 bindings & dynamic pricing hooks

open_questions.q: Would fitting per-SKU popularity and basket-size distributions into the C++ shopper state machines close the 38% top-10 SKU overlap gap, and how does the engine calibrate against real (non-synthetic) store POS exports?
open_questions.resolves: Calibrating on real retail POS transactions (out of scope for v1 closure; PriceRiot v1 is closed).

projects.name: QSR ERP
projects.subtitle: Relational SQLite ERP schema, fail-fast modular Flask framework, and team architecture lead
projects.summary: Architected the normalized SQLite data contract (sales, recipes, inventory, scheduling, double-booking trigger, reporting views), deterministic 4-week seed generator, and PBKDF2/RBAC/CSRF Flask screen loader for a multi-developer ERP team.
projects.meta: Architecture & Team Lead · SQLite / SQL · Flask · CSUF ISDS 454

case_study.problem: Multi-developer enterprise applications break down when teams write ad-hoc queries without enforced relational invariants, auth checks, or clean module boundaries. QSR ERP puts schema constraints, reporting views, auth/CSRF guards, and fail-fast screen registration in a single shared foundation.

flow.title: Team Screen Modules & Operational POSTs
flow.detail: Independent feature folders register screens for sales imports, inventory/recipes, scheduling, and threshold alerts.

flow.title: Fail-Fast Loader, Auth/CSRF & SQLite Triggers
flow.detail: Screen loader halts startup on broken modules; PBKDF2 login, role guards, and CSRF check every POST; SQLite constraints and triggers block double-booking.

flow.title: Transactional Ledger & Reporting Views
flow.detail: Commits valid operational rows and serves pre-joined SQL reporting views for team BI screens, or rejects invalid writes.

case_study.tradeoff: The relational schema, reporting views, deterministic 4-week seed generator, and Flask framework are built on main (30 commits), while teammates' feature screens remain in progress ahead of feature freeze. All current rows are generated sample data, and parked extensions (break-even simulator, database-grounded AI summaries, live POS onboarding) remain design-only.

open_questions.q: Do the required screens land before the feature freeze?
open_questions.resolves: The team's screens merged to main.

projects.name: TunedIn
projects.subtitle: Layered .NET 8 desktop ticketing architecture with decoupled core domain and service layer
projects.summary: Structured a multi-screen desktop ticketing workflow (login, ticket-pack selection, cart, payment, receipts) over a separated ISDS309.Core domain/services library backed by delimited flat-file persistence.
projects.meta: C# / .NET 8 WinForms · Layered Architecture · CSUF ISDS 309

case_study.problem: Small desktop applications often couple UI forms directly to storage files, making workflows brittle to extend. TunedIn separates domain models, enums, and ticketing services into a shared .NET 8 core library beneath the WinForms screens.

flow.title: WinForms Ticketing Screens
flow.detail: Captures user actions across login, ticket-pack selection, cart management, and checkout screens.

flow.title: ISDS309.Core Domain & Services
flow.detail: Isolates domain entities, status enums, and cart/payment service logic from form event handlers.

flow.title: Receipts & Delimited File Storage
flow.detail: Generates order receipts and writes state to comma-delimited text files (with explicitly documented reliability gaps).

case_study.tradeoff: Built as an earlier desktop systems project and published with its known README limitations intact: login does not check credentials against stored user records, state is not auto-saved on exit, the main loop lacks top-level error handling, and the directory was not kept under Git version control.

open_questions.q: Were the README's known gaps ever closed?
open_questions.resolves: A credential check against stored users and a save on exit.

ai_disclosure.tagline: AI coding assistants helped build this site. Here is which models were used, how I reviewed and iterated on every output, and where the boundary sits.

sections.heading: Models used
sections.intro: Two model families were used as coding and editing assistants while building and hosting this site:
items: Claude (Anthropic): initial static site generator, candidate ledger extraction from local repositories and notes, and visual restyling.
Gemini (Google): EndeavourOS Beelink hosting setup, container and deployment fixes, and follow-up site edits.

sections.heading: Where AI helped
sections.intro: AI coding assistants were used as build and editing tools for the site itself:
items: Static site generator: drafting and iterating on build.py, portfolio/render.py, portfolio/validate.py, CSS layout, and verify/verify.py.
Ledger assembly: extracting candidate entries, commit hashes, and file paths from local repositories and notes into content/ledger.yaml for review.
Hosting and deployment: writing Docker, Caddy, Cloudflare Tunnel, systemd, and GitHub Actions configs under infra/ and .github/workflows/.
Prose drafting: initial wording for navigation, layout copy, and repository documentation.

sections.heading: Review and iteration
paragraphs: No generated output went live unreviewed. I checked each page, wording pass, and ledger entry myself and iterated through many rounds of revision before publishing.

Earlier passes were discarded or reworked when the visual style looked generic, when narrow screens overflowed, when prose overstated what the evidence supported, or when hosting configs failed live checks. Every revision still had to pass the validator test suite, deterministic build, and verification script before deploying.

sections.heading: What AI does not decide
sections.intro: The factual record and publication gates do not rest on model output:
items: Build-time checks: every claim renders from content/ledger.yaml and is checked deterministically by build.py and verify/verify.py. A MEASURED entry fails the build without explicit metrics, denominators, datasets, and evidence pointers; a LINKED entry requires a file path, branch, and commit SHA.
Visible uncertainty: unverified statements are labeled AUTHOR-REPORTED, STALE (older than 90 days), or UNKNOWN rather than filled in with generated prose.
Author direction: I chose the visual direction, scope, which entries are public or hidden, and what gets published.

sections.heading: Why state this here
paragraphs: My work is about AI verification and grounding: systems where a model may propose, but a deterministic check decides what gets admitted.

Applying that same rule to the portfolio means stating plainly which models assisted, how their output was reviewed across iterations, and letting the ledger, commit hashes, and build checks carry the evidence instead of prose.
